title.en: Commutators and conjugates as piece tools

summary: Build move sequences that touch few pieces and show why the algebraic form produces that effect.
objective: Build a cube workbench where I can assemble a commutator or a conjugate from chosen moves and see exactly which pieces it disturbs.
intent_signals: Show how a commutator affects only a few pieces.
Explain conjugation as setup, algorithm and undo.
example_prompts: Build a cube tool that assembles commutators and conjugates and lists the pieces each one moves.
Show a three-cycle produced by a commutator and where its setup moves point it.
negative_signals: Not a solver: this recipe builds and inspects sequences, it does not search for solutions.
Not a speedcubing method trainer or algorithm database.
not_for: Not a solver: this recipe builds and inspects sequences, it does not search for solutions.
Not a speedcubing method trainer or algorithm database.

entities.name: Move slots
entities.guidance: Provide explicit slots for the two operand sequences so the algebraic form stays visible instead of collapsing into one string.

entities.name: Affected piece report
entities.guidance: After applying a sequence, list every piece whose position or orientation changed, since that count is the whole point of the construction.

entities.name: Inverse preview
entities.guidance: Show the inverse of each operand as generated text, so the structure of the commutator or conjugate is verifiable.

state_contract.model: Exact discrete puzzle state as piece positions and orientations, plus a sequence builder with one declared composition convention used everywhere in this record: sequences are written left to right in execution order, so g h means apply g and then h. Under that convention this record uses the commutator [g, h] = g h g inverse h inverse (apply g, then h, then g inverse, then h inverse) and the conjugate of g by h = h g h inverse (setup h, apply g, undo h). Texts that write the commutator as g inverse h inverse g h and the conjugate as h inverse g h name a different word, and which word depends on their composition order: read right to left (rightmost applied first) g inverse h inverse g h executes as h, g, h inverse, g inverse, which is [h, g] = [g, h] inverse, the inverse commutator; read left to right, as the cited Jaap Scherphuis page does because its permutations act on the right, the same text executes as g inverse, h inverse, g, h, which is [g inverse, h inverse] here. Build and label sequences with the form written in this record and never mix the two texts. Move notation and sequence length are validated before application. Animation is presentation only.
state_contract.authority: The discrete state is authoritative; the animated mesh follows it. A sequence is judged by the state difference it produces, never by how it looks.
actions: Choose the two operand sequences and apply the commutator.
Wrap any sequence in a conjugating setup and its inverse.
Inspect the list of affected pieces.
Undo the whole construction and reset to solved.

invariants: Applying a sequence and then its inverse returns the exact original state, including orientations.
The affected piece list is computed from the state difference, not from what was animated.
A conjugate moves the same pattern of pieces as its inner sequence, relocated by the setup.
motion_guidance: Animate each move as a quarter or half turn of the correct layer and keep the discrete state as the source of truth.
Allow stepping backwards through the built sequence; a construction that can only be watched cannot be understood.
known_limits: Effect size depends on the operands chosen: not every commutator produces a small three-cycle.
This recipe covers construction and inspection, not the search for a sequence with a desired effect.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The cited page defines a conjugate of g as h inverse g h and the commutator of g and h as g inverse h inverse g h, composing left to right because its permutations act on the right, and states that taking a commutator of two elements that nearly commute yields a sequence that moves very little. In the convention declared by this record those two source words are the same constructions on inverted operands: the source commutator is this record's [g inverse, h inverse] and the source conjugate is this record's conjugate of g by h inverse.
claims.scope: Group-theoretic definitions applied to puzzle move sequences as cited. The word order depends on the composition convention: the cited page composes left to right, while texts composing right to left read the same word g inverse h inverse g h as the execution sequence h, g, h inverse, g inverse, which is the inverse commutator [h, g]. This record declares one convention in its state contract and builds only the forms written under it.

source_refs.locator: Section 7, Conjugation and commutation: "a conjugate of g is an element h-1gh" and "the commutator of g and h is the element g-1h-1gh", with permutations acting on the right

claims.statement: If a move sequence swaps, cycles, flips or twists particular pieces, then conjugates of that sequence apply the same kind of effect to other pieces.
claims.scope: Practical consequence of conjugation as cited; the relocation is determined by the setup sequence.

source_refs.locator: Section 7, after Lemma 7.1: "if you have a move sequence that swaps/cycles/flips/twists some particular pieces, then using conjugates of that move sequence you can swap/cycle/flip/twist any other pieces you want"

object_craft.structure: Physical slot rails in the scene holding move tiles, so a sequence is an object that can be reordered.
object_craft.material: Tiles with printed notation and a face-colour edge, readable at the working camera distance.
object_craft.articulation: Tiles can be inserted, removed and reordered; the generated inverse updates immediately.

object_craft.structure: Ghost markers on the cube at every changed piece plus a side list with piece names.
object_craft.material: One reserved accent for changed pieces so an unchanged cube reads as visually quiet.
object_craft.articulation: Markers rebuild from the state difference after each application.

physical_contract.scope: Exact discrete state with animated layer turns; no friction, contact or mechanism simulation.
checks: Sequence followed by its inverse restores the exact state.
The affected piece list matches the computed state difference.
